As a [stakeholder]: Normal Student / Advising Student / Advisor / Coordinator / Administrator
I should be able to [action]: log in using my GUC email and password
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: There is no sign-up. Credentials already exist in the database. Advisor, Coordinator and Administrator emails end in @guc.edu.eg. Student emails end in @student.guc.edu.eg. Only active accounts may log in.

As a [stakeholder]: Normal Student / Advising Student / Advisor / Coordinator / Administrator
I should be able to [action]: reset my password using a one-time password sent to my GUC email

As a [stakeholder]: Normal Student / Advising Student / Advisor / Coordinator / Administrator
I should be able to [action]: log out from the system

As a [stakeholder]: Normal Student / Advising Student / Advisor / Coordinator / Administrator
I should be able to [action]: view my profile information applicable to my role
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: Every user sees their full name, GUC email and role. Student profiles also show student ID, student type, major, current semester, academic standing, assigned Advisor when applicable and schedule status. Each user may view only their own profile.

As a [stakeholder]: Normal Student / Advising Student / Advisor / Coordinator / Administrator
I should be able to [action]: view my in-app notifications and mark them as read
view a list of all GUC students and their current scheduling workflow status
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: The list includes Normal Students and Advising Students and shows full name, GUC email, student ID, student type, major, current semester, assigned Advisor when applicable, workflow status, blocking step and last update time. The status is calculated from completed workflow actions; Advisors do not manually overwrite it. Normal-student statuses include Schedule Assigned, Swap Request Open, Swap Completed, Swap Withdrawn and Swap Expired. Advising-student statuses include Not Started, Draft, Ready for Student Review, Change Request Pending, Pending Approval, Awaiting Payment Choice, Deferred to Next Installment, Ready to Process, Processed and Reopened.

I should be able to [action]: search for a GUC student using the student ID, full name or GUC email
filter GUC students by student type, assigned Advisor, major, current semester, academic standing, workflow status, blocking step and account status
view and select a GUC student from the displayed search or filter results to open the student's details
activate or deactivate a user account
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: Deactivation prevents login without deleting the user's academic, scheduling or audit history.

I should be able to [action]: add an advisor using the advisor's GUC email
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: When a valid email is entered, the advisor's full name is displayed.

I should be able to [action]: remove an advisor from the advising system using the advisor's GUC email
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: Removing an advisor does not delete the advisor's previous actions from the schedule activity history.

I should be able to [action]: receive an email when I am added to or removed from the advising system
assign or reassign an advisor to an advising student
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: Reassignment preserves the student's schedule, requests, plans and advisor history.

I should be able to [action]: view the name and GUC email of my assigned advisor
create an academic term and define its registration and advising-season dates
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: The dates include the term start and end, teaching start and end, advising deadline and normal-student whole-schedule-swap deadline. Affected actions are blocked after their applicable deadline.

I should be able to [action]: update an academic term and its registration and advising-season dates
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: The dates include the term start and end, teaching start and end, advising deadline and normal-student whole-schedule-swap deadline. Affected actions are blocked after their applicable deadline.

I should be able to [action]: create a course in the course catalogue
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: Each course includes its code, name, credit hours, course type (core, elective, huma), faculty/major, recommended semester, offering season and prerequisites. Electives are managed through the same course catalogue. Refer to the MET and DMET Curriculum sheet.

I should be able to [action]: view the course catalogue and the details of each course
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: Each course includes its code, name, credit hours, course type (core, elective, huma),faculty/major, recommended semester, offering season and prerequisites. Electives are managed through the same course catalogue. Refer to the MET and DMET Curriculum sheet.

I should be able to [action]: update a course in the course catalogue
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: Each course includes its code, name, credit hours, course type (core, elective, huma), faculty/major, recommended semester, offering season and prerequisites. Electives are managed through the same course catalogue. Refer to the MET and DMET Curriculum sheet.

I should be able to [action]: delete a course from the course catalogue
create a course offering and its lecture, tutorial and lab slots
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: A course offering is a catalogue course delivered in one academic term. It includes the academic year and term, assigned instructor(s), eligible major/semester groups, publication status, and all lecture, tutorial and lab groups. Every group records its type, group number, day, start and end times, room, maximum capacity, assigned-student count and system-calculated remaining capacity. A course without a published offering in the selected term cannot be scheduled. Refer to the MET and DMET Curriculum sheet.

I should be able to [action]: view course offerings for an academic term and select an offering to view all of its details and slots
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: A course offering is a catalogue course delivered in one academic term. It includes the academic year and term, assigned instructor(s), eligible major/semester groups, publication status, and all lecture, tutorial and lab groups. Every group records its type, group number, day, start and end times, room, maximum capacity, assigned-student count and system-calculated remaining capacity. A course without a published offering in the selected term cannot be scheduled. Refer to the MET and DMET Curriculum sheet.

I should be able to [action]: duplicate course offerings from a selected previous Winter, Spring or Summer term into a target academic term
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: The Administrator selects the source academic year and season and an existing target term. The system copies the offered courses, assigned instructors, eligible major and semester groups, and lecture, tutorial and lab group structures including their days, times, rooms and maximum capacities. Every copy is created as an unpublished draft in the target term. Do not copy enrolled students, assigned-student counts, remaining-capacity values, schedule assignments, swap or change requests, publication status or activity history. Recalculate remaining capacity from the copied maximum capacity, flag room or instructor conflicts, and skip rather than overwrite any course offering that already exists in the target term. The Administrator must review and publish the copied offerings before scheduling uses them.

I should be able to [action]: update a course offering or one of its lecture, tutorial or lab slots
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: A course offering is a catalogue course delivered in one academic term. It includes the academic year and term, assigned instructor(s), eligible major/semester groups, publication status, and all lecture, tutorial and lab groups. Every group records its type, group number, day, start and end times, room, maximum capacity, assigned-student count and system-calculated remaining capacity. A course without a published offering in the selected term cannot be scheduled. Updating a slot must not create a timetable conflict or reduce capacity below its assigned-student count. Refer to the MET and DMET Curriculum sheet.

I should be able to [action]: delete a course offering or one of its lecture, tutorial or lab slots
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: A course offering is a catalogue course delivered in one academic term. It includes the academic year and term, assigned instructor(s), eligible major/semester groups, publication status, and all lecture, tutorial and lab groups. Every group records its type, group number, day, start and end times, room, maximum capacity, assigned-student count and system-calculated remaining capacity. A course without a published offering in the selected term cannot be scheduled. An offering or slot with assigned students cannot be deleted until those assignments are moved or removed. Refer to the MET and DMET Curriculum sheet.

I should be able to [action]: publish or unpublish course offerings for a term
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: Only published offerings appear during schedule creation, graduation planning or slot-change requests. Unpublishing is blocked when it would invalidate an active or processed schedule.

I should be able to [action]: create a standard schedule template for normal students by major, semester and study group
update a standard schedule template for normal students by major, semester and study group
assign or reassign normal students to a standard schedule group
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: A student's processed schedule is created from the assigned group's published template.

As a [stakeholder]: Normal Student / Advising Student / Advisor / Coordinator / Administrator
I should be able to [action]: view a student's current weekly schedule including course code, course name, lecture, tutorial and lab times and locations
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: A Normal Student may view only their own processed standard schedule. An Advising Student may view their own completed draft after an Advisor or Coordinator marks it Ready for Student Review, and may continue to view the final processed schedule. A completed draft has every required course and lecture, tutorial and lab slot assigned, has no blocking validation issue, and is not yet final. Incomplete drafts remain hidden from the student. Advisors and Coordinators may view an advising student's draft, review-ready or processed schedule, and Administrators have read-only access. The schedule is displayed as a weekly calendar and shows days off.

I should be able to [action]: view my registered courses, the credit hours of each course and my total registered credit hours
select a registered course and view its assigned lecture, tutorial and lab details
view eligible destination group numbers and their complete weekly schedules for a whole-schedule swap
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: Show only standard schedule groups for the same term whose registered course-code set exactly matches the student's subjects, with no additional or missing subject. Display each group number and its complete lecture, tutorial and lab schedule.

I should be able to [action]: submit a whole-schedule swap request by selecting one or more desired group numbers before the deadline
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: The system auto-populates the student's current group number and complete current schedule from the processed record; the student cannot edit them. The student selects one or more eligible desired groups and may have only one active swap request.

I should be able to [action]: view open whole-schedule swap requests that I am eligible to complete
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: A request is visible only when the viewer's current group is one of the requester's desired groups, both students have the exact same registered course-code set and term, and both schedules are processed. Show the requester's current group, complete schedule and desired group options, but do not reveal the requester's identity.

I should be able to [action]: complete an eligible open whole-schedule swap request and move into the requester's current group
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: Immediately before completion, revalidate the deadline, request status, desired-group membership, exact subject match, term and both processed schedules. Then atomically exchange the two students' group assignments and every lecture, tutorial and lab slot. Do not apply a partial swap or change either student's registered subjects. Only the first valid completion may succeed.

I should be able to [action]: view my submitted or completed whole-schedule swap requests, their group details and statuses
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: Statuses are Open, Completed, Withdrawn and Expired.

I should be able to [action]: withdraw my own open whole-schedule swap request
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: A completed, withdrawn or expired request cannot be withdrawn.

I should be able to [action]: request a change to one assigned lecture, tutorial or lab slot in my completed schedule before it is processed and include an optional preference note
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: This action is available only while the completed schedule is Ready for Student Review and before the advising deadline. The request identifies the course, component type and current slot. The preference note may mention a preferred group or day. The student cannot directly change the slot.

I should be able to [action]: view my slot-change requests, their statuses and the Advisor or Coordinator response
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: Statuses are Pending, Approved, Rejected and Withdrawn. The response identifies any approved replacement slot.

I should be able to [action]: withdraw my pending slot-change request
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: Only a Pending request may be withdrawn. A request that has already been approved, rejected or withdrawn cannot be withdrawn again.

I should be able to [action]: view a list of advising-student slot-change requests
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: An Advisor sees requests from assigned advising students. A Coordinator may see all advising-student requests.

I should be able to [action]: search advising-student slot-change requests using a student ID, student name or course code
filter advising-student slot-change requests by request status, Advisor, course and submission date
view and select an advising-student slot-change request from the displayed search or filter results to open its details
compare the student's current slot with available alternatives, remaining seats and timetable clashes
approve or reject an advising-student slot-change request and provide an optional response note
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: Approval selects the exact replacement slot. Revalidate capacity and timetable clashes, then update the completed schedule and both slot capacities atomically so the same final seat cannot be assigned twice. The schedule remains Ready for Student Review until all pending requests are resolved and it is processed.

I should be able to [action]: download or print my processed schedule
view a list of advising students
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: Advisors can view all advising students, including students assigned to other Advisors. Show each student's assigned Advisor, workflow status, blocking step and last update time. Student IDs use the XX-XXXX format, for example 64-12345.

I should be able to [action]: search for an advising student using the student ID, full name or GUC email
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: Search covers all advising students. Student IDs use the XX-XXXX format, for example 64-12345.

I should be able to [action]: filter advising students by Advisor, major, advising reason, schedule status and pending-request type
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: Filters may be combined and cleared. An Advisor can choose themselves in the Advisor filter to display 'My assigned students', but may also view students assigned to other Advisors.

I should be able to [action]: view and select an advising student from the displayed search or filter results to open the student's advising details
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: Any Advisor may open a student from the displayed results to view the academic and advising information permitted by the remaining requirements.

I should be able to [action]: view a student's academic history organized into completed courses with grades, current courses and remaining courses
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: Show the student's Advisor, major, GPA, completed hours and current semester. Every remaining course shows its credit hours, prerequisites and offering season. An Advising Student may view only their own academic history. Advisors and Coordinators may view any advising student.

I should be able to [action]: select an attended academic year and view the corresponding transcript
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: The transcript includes Winter, Spring, Summer, first-makeup and second-makeup results where applicable. An Advising Student may view only their own transcript.

I should be able to [action]: download the displayed transcript as a PDF
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: An Advising Student may download only their own transcript.

I should be able to [action]: submit or update my scheduling preferences before the advising deadline
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: Preferences may include preferred or avoided days, preferred or avoided time ranges, preferred groups, desired days off and an optional note. The student may rank preferences by priority. Preferences are not guaranteed and cannot override mandatory courses, prerequisites, published offerings, capacity, timetable-clash rules, credit-hour limits or approved extra-hour rules.

I should be able to [action]: view an advising student's submitted scheduling preferences while creating or updating the draft schedule
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: Show the latest submitted preferences, their priority order and last update time. The Advisor or Coordinator may satisfy them when feasible but must preserve all academic and scheduling rules. A student who submitted no preferences may still receive a schedule.

I should be able to [action]: view an advising student's advising reason, system-calculated credit-hour allowance, schedule status and bachelor-project eligibility
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: Advising reasons are probation, more than two failed courses in a season, unattended courses, undeclared CS or DMET major, or transfer from another major/university. Standard allowances are 34 hours for semesters 3-4, 30 for semesters 5-6, 28 for semester 7, and 24 from semester 8 onward. On the GUC scale, probation is GPA 3.70 or above; probation students receive 25% less hours than normal student (any decimal points to be rounded up) hours and cannot receive an increase. Workflow status is calculated automatically from the student's draft, pending approvals, settlement decision and processing actions; it is not manually selected by an Advisor. Bachelor-project eligibility requires completion of all courses from semesters 1-6 and all English courses including RPW. A student with only one or two failed courses from semesters 1-6 remains eligible if all English courses including RPW are complete.

I should be able to [action]: add the bachelor project to an eligible student's schedule and select whether it will be taken in Winter or Spring
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: A bachelor student may take up to four courses with the project: at most two core courses and two humanities. Humanities are German courses, Seminar, Introduction to Management and Project Management. These courses are treated as extra hours and follow the extra-hours approval and payment flow.

I should be able to [action]: view an advising student's failed and unattended courses as mandatory-course candidates
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: Failed and unattended courses are mandatory unless an approved removal applies.

I should be able to [action]: create an open draft schedule for an advising student
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: Display any submitted scheduling preferences while the draft is created. Preferences are optional and their absence does not block schedule creation.

I should be able to [action]: select the mandatory courses to include in an advising student's schedule
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: Mandatory courses are selected before other courses and consume the student's available credit hours. If mandatory courses consume all allowed hours, no other course may be added without approved extra hours.

I should be able to [action]: request the removal of a mandatory course and provide the reason
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: Valid cases include an incorrect mandatory designation due to first- or second-makeup eligibility, or deferral when the student completed more than 157 hours or would otherwise take restricted pairs of CS, Math or Physics courses in the same term. Students always receive a first makeup. A second makeup is available only when the student has one or two failed courses.

I should be able to [action]: view a list of mandatory-course removal requests
search mandatory-course removal requests using a student ID, course code or Advisor's name or GUC email
filter mandatory-course removal requests by Advisor, request status and submission date
view and select a mandatory-course removal request from the displayed search or filter results to open its details
approve or reject a mandatory-course removal request and provide a response note
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: Approval removes the course from the mandatory list and any unprocessed draft schedule. Rejection leaves it mandatory.

I should be able to [action]: view the other courses an advising student is eligible to take in the selected term
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: Exclude completed courses, courses with unmet prerequisites and courses not offered in the selected season. Eligibility follows the student's semester progression and published course offerings.

I should be able to [action]: add an eligible non-mandatory course to an advising student's draft schedule
remove a non-mandatory course from an advising student's draft schedule
view the selected, allowed, extra and remaining credit hours while building an advising student's schedule
save an advising student's incomplete schedule as a draft and continue editing it later
select a chosen course and view its available lecture, tutorial and lab slots with remaining capacities
assign a student's lecture, tutorial and lab slots for a selected course
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: The action must prevent overlapping slots and must update remaining capacity atomically so two users cannot take the same final seat.

I should be able to [action]: change a student's assigned lecture, tutorial or lab slot
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: The action must prevent overlapping slots and must update remaining capacity atomically so two users cannot take the same final seat.

I should be able to [action]: remove a student's assigned lecture, tutorial or lab slot
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: The action must prevent overlapping slots and must update remaining capacity atomically so two users cannot take the same final seat.

I should be able to [action]: view all validation issues in a draft schedule before processing it
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: Validation covers missing mandatory courses, missing required slots, prerequisites, unpublished offerings, timetable clashes, capacity and allowed or approved credit hours.

I should be able to [action]: mark a completed and valid advising schedule as Ready for Student Review
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: The action is allowed only when every required course and lecture, tutorial and lab slot is assigned and no blocking validation issue remains. It gives the Advising Student read-only access to the completed schedule and enables pre-processing slot-change requests.

I should be able to [action]: process a valid advising schedule
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: Processing finalizes the schedule. It is blocked while any slot-change request is Pending or while a required approval or payment choice remains unresolved. After processing, the student may view and download the final schedule but cannot submit a new pre-processing slot-change request.

I should be able to [action]: reopen a processed advising schedule and provide a reason
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: Reopening returns the schedule to Draft status and hides it from the student until it is completed, validated and marked Ready for Student Review again. A reason is required.

I should be able to [action]: request extra credit hours for an advising student and specify the courses and requested hours
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: Probation students cannot receive extra hours. Other students may not exceed 34 total hours. A student not graduating within one year may add at most three hours above the standard allowance. A student graduating within one year may add hours up to the 34-hour maximum. Repeated-course hours cost EGP 1,000 each; new-course hours cost EGP 800 each.

I should be able to [action]: view all extra-hours requests and their details
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: Each request shows the student, requesting Advisor, requested courses and hours, eligibility checks, itemized cost, Coordinator decision, settlement status and submission date.

I should be able to [action]: search extra-hours requests using a student ID
filter extra-hours requests by requesting Advisor, Coordinator decision, settlement option and settlement status
approve or reject an extra-hours request and provide a response note
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: Approval confirms the eligibility rules and itemized cost, then makes the request available for the student to settle. Approval alone does not activate the extra hours or add the courses to the usable schedule.

I should be able to [action]: view a Coordinator-approved extra-hours request with its courses, credit hours, price per hour, subtotals and total cost
view my wallet balance and wallet transaction history
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: The history shows refund credits and payment debits with the amount, date, related request or payment, and resulting balance.

I should be able to [action]: choose to pay an approved extra-hours request now or add its amount to my next university installment
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: The request remains Awaiting Payment Choice until one option is confirmed.

I should be able to [action]: choose my wallet or a third-party payment gateway and pay the approved extra-hours amount now
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: Wallet payment requires a sufficient balance; split payments are not required. The gateway is a sandbox, and the platform must not store card numbers, CVVs or gateway passwords. Apply the approved hours and courses only after successful payment.

I should be able to [action]: confirm that the approved extra-hours amount will be added to my next university installment
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: Confirmation creates an outstanding deferred charge linked to the next installment and immediately activates the approved hours and courses. The amount must not also be charged to the wallet or gateway.

I should be able to [action]: retry a failed or cancelled third-party gateway payment
view and download a payment receipt or deferred-payment confirmation
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: A paid receipt includes the payment method and transaction reference. A deferred-payment confirmation includes the related installment, amount due and confirmation date and must not be labelled as a paid receipt.

I should be able to [action]: view the status and decision history of an extra-hours request
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: The history shows the Coordinator decision and whether the request is Awaiting Payment Choice, Paid, Deferred to Next Installment, Failed, Cancelled or Refunded.

I should be able to [action]: withdraw an extra-hours request before Coordinator approval
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: An approved, rejected, paid or deferred request cannot be withdrawn. Approved requests use the cancellation or refund flow.

I should be able to [action]: view my extra-hours payment and deferred-charge history including each record's settlement option and status
view a list of extra-hours financial records
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: Each record shows the student, request, amount, settlement option, transaction or deferred-charge reference, relevant date and status.

I should be able to [action]: search extra-hours financial records using a student ID, request ID, transaction reference or deferred-charge reference
filter extra-hours financial records by date, settlement option and status
view and select an extra-hours financial record from the displayed search or filter results to open its details
refund a paid extra-hours charge or cancel an unpaid deferred charge for an eligible cancelled request
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: A paid amount is refunded to the student's wallet and cannot be refunded twice. An unpaid deferred charge is removed from the next installment without crediting the wallet. In both cases, revoke the related extra hours and unapplied schedule additions and retain the reversal history.

I should be able to [action]: create a graduation plan and assign every remaining course to the next Winter, Spring or Summer term
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: Every remaining course must be assigned. Course offering seasons and prerequisite order must be respected. Each term must remain within the student's standard or separately approved credit-hour limit. An approved exit exam may replace the single failed course covered by that approval.

I should be able to [action]: update a graduation plan that I created while it is still a draft
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: A submitted plan cannot be updated.

I should be able to [action]: delete a graduation plan that I created while it is still a draft
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: A submitted plan cannot be deleted.

I should be able to [action]: save an unfinished graduation plan as a private draft
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: A draft is visible only to the Advisor who created it. It is not visible to the Coordinator, student or other Advisors until submitted.

I should be able to [action]: submit a finalized graduation plan
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: Submission is allowed only when every remaining course is assigned to the next Winter, Spring or Summer term, or when the only unassigned failed course has an approved exit-exam request. The submitted plan becomes read-only while awaiting the Coordinator's decision.

I should be able to [action]: request an exit exam for an advising student who has exactly one remaining failed course that cannot be repeated before graduation
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: The request identifies the course and explains why it cannot be placed in the next Winter, Spring or Summer term, such as the course not being offered or no valid placement remaining.

I should be able to [action]: approve or reject an exit-exam request and provide a response note
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: Approval allows the course to be represented by an exit exam in the graduation plan. Rejection requires the Advisor to place the course in a valid term before submitting the plan.

I should be able to [action]: view submitted graduation plans and their statuses
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: An Advisor sees plans they submitted. A Coordinator sees all submitted plans. Private drafts remain visible only to their creating Advisor.

I should be able to [action]: filter submitted graduation plans by status, Advisor and submission date
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: Private drafts are excluded because they are visible only to their creating Advisor.

I should be able to [action]: search submitted graduation plans using a student ID or Advisor's name or GUC email
accept or reject a submitted graduation plan and provide a response note
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: Acceptance confirms that the student can complete the remaining graduation requirements within one year. Rejection returns the plan to its creating Advisor as a private draft that can be corrected and resubmitted.

I should be able to [action]: view my accepted graduation plan
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: The plan becomes visible to the student only after Coordinator acceptance.

I should be able to [action]: view the status and Coordinator response for an exit-exam request submitted for me
connect my account to a supported third-party calendar using OAuth and synchronize my processed schedule
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: Support at least one provider, such as Google Calendar or Microsoft Outlook Calendar. The platform must not request or store the calendar password. Create recurring events for the teaching period using the university timezone. Each event includes course code and name, slot type, time, room and instructor when available.

I should be able to [action]: receive notifications about open or completed group-based schedule swaps, advising schedule review and slot-change decisions, schedule processing or reopening, extra-hours decisions, payments, deferred charges, refunds, graduation-plan decisions and exit-exam decisions
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: Only events relevant to the student's type and own requests are sent.

I should be able to [action]: receive a warning email after remaining on probation for two consecutive semesters
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: The email is sent to the student's GUC email after the second consecutive probation semester. It warns that if the student does not leave probation in the following semester, the student may be exposed to termination from the university.

I should be able to [action]: receive notifications when I am assigned an advising student or when an assigned student submits or withdraws a slot-change request
receive notifications when a graduation plan is submitted or when an exit-exam, mandatory-course removal, extra-hours or financial-reversal request requires action
receive reminders before the advising deadline for assigned schedules that remain open
view a pending-work dashboard showing every student's workflow status, blocking step and requests awaiting action, grouped by student type, request type and Advisor
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: Statuses are system-derived from completed actions and cannot be manually overwritten by an Advisor. The dashboard includes open and completed normal-student group swaps and advising-student draft, review, change-request, approval, settlement and processing states.

I should be able to [action]: view the automatically recorded history of schedule processing and reopening actions
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: The system records entries automatically. From a selected student's advising details, show that student's history; from the global history page, show all advising students. Each entry shows the student ID, action, schedule version, staff member's full name, GUC email and role, date and time, and reopening reason when applicable.

I should be able to [action]: filter the schedule activity history by action type and date range
search the schedule activity history using a student ID or staff member's name or GUC email
export the displayed schedule activity history
export filtered extra-hours financial records
import multiple course records into the course catalogue from a CSV file
Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST: The CSV includes course code, name, credit hours, course type (core, elective, huma), faculty/major, recommended semester, offering season and prerequisites. Before importing, the system validates the required columns and values and shows row-level errors. New course codes are created and existing course codes are updated without creating duplicates. If any row is invalid, no rows are imported until the file is corrected.
